A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same federated cross-graph query-answering work, renamed from FedCQA to FedNGDB. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments on FB15k-237, FB15k, and NELL995, including three- and five-client comparisons and query-type analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds communication-round, ten-client, and overlapping-relation results in Table 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 4.1.1 and Algorithm 1 add explicit homomorphic encryption of perturbed uploads, encrypted server aggregation, and client decryption. v1's algorithm specified masking and encrypted mask sharing without these HE steps. The base encoders, masking scheme, operator aggregation, and query-retrieval design remain.

E1.justification: The three datasets and eight logical query types remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 adds evaluation with overlapping relation types across clients, extending the previously evaluated nonoverlapping-relation scenario. The LLM/RAG motivation introduces no evaluated LLM task.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain Local, Central, FedE, and FedR with GQE, Q2P, and Tree-LSTM. The added convergence comparison reuses FedE and FedR, while Appendix C reuses Local; no comparison method is added or removed from the retained experiments.

E3.justification: New evaluations use ten clients with GQE, randomly split data among three clients for relation overlap, and measure communication rounds relative to FedE. Existing three- and five-client protocols, 8:1:1 splits, query counts, embedding dimensions, optimizer, and retrieval metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 adds a focused convergence-efficiency comparison. Appendix C tests whether retrieval benefits persist with ten clients and overlapping relations. These supplement the retained query-type and per-client analyses without adding component ablations or privacy-attack evaluations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run variability. Existing client averages and the new point estimates do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 and Figure 4 retain their numerical results. New Tables 5–7 add communication-round ratios of 1.00, 1.32, and 1.09 for FedE, FedR, and FedNGDB, plus GQE results for ten clients and relation overlap. For example, ten-client FB15k-237 MRR is 8.46 for Local versus 10.17 for FedNGDB.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 newly states the privacy assumption that entity and relation indices may be shared while triples are sensitive. The logical-query definitions, Equations 1–7, and underlying key-exchange reasoning remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain federated complex query answering, privacy protection, and a three-dataset benchmark. v3 broadens the stated application scope to neural graph databases and promotes efficient retrieval for LLM-related applications, without adding an LLM evaluation.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies privacy protection by allowing entity and relation indices to be shared. It also interprets the new communication-round results as competitive efficiency alongside privacy protection and the appendix results as evidence of applicability with more clients and shared relations.

D1.justification: Section 4.2.1 expands execution details: the server routes atomic queries to corresponding clients, collects their encodings, and iterates communication until the query is encoded. This documents the retained retrieval design more explicitly. Existing hyperparameter and optimizer information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The research positioning expands substantially from complex query answering and federated KG embeddings to neural graph databases, federated databases, and LLM/RAG applications. Added references include Neural Graph Databases, SMCQL, graph-driven federated data management, and RAG research, while the earlier CQA and embedding literature is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and opening introduction are substantially rewritten around neural graph databases and LLM/RAG retrieval. The title, terminology, and related-work headings change throughout; query-execution explanations expand, Appendix B gains subsections, and the roadmap and acknowledgments are removed.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with embedding-storage and query-engine elements, and Figure 2 is relabeled and adjusted. Algorithm 1 moves from the main text to Appendix B, and Tables 5–7 are added. The main result-table structures and query/result figures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v3 makes privacy assumptions and encrypted aggregation more explicit and adds useful evidence about communication rounds, ten-client operation, and relation overlap. These provide limited gains in clarity and empirical support. The gains are constrained by sparse protocol details for the new tests and an expanded LLM/RAG framing without corresponding evaluation; the principal retrieval results remain unchanged.
